title: Pemberton TravelOps outbound sketch
body:
Prospect snapshot:
- Company: Pemberton TravelOps (small-to-mid travel SaaS, B2B2C).
- HQ: Boston. Estimated 400 employees, engineering + ops heavy.
- Product: booking + itineraries + 24/7 customer support chat + personalized offers.
- Current infra hints: AWS + EKS, in-house search, using OpenAI-like hosted APIs for experiments (public threads / job posts mention latency pain).

Why this fits Redwood: quick win with inference economics and reliability. They need predictable latency for customer chat + embedding search for itineraries; cost is becoming a gating factor as volume grows. Regulatory risk is moderate (PCI adjacency), but data classification calls for ops control and auditability.

Key stakeholders to target (hypothesis):
- Leah Armstrong — VP Product (owner for personalization / search)
- Marco Ruiz — Head of Platform (infra, procurement)
- Naomi Kline — Director of Customer Ops (chatbot owner)
- CTO/Engineering manager (purchase champion)

Primary use cases to pitch:
1) Agent/chat support: reduce time-to-first-token (latency) and increase concurrency with predictable SLOs.
2) Embedding-based itinerary search: cheaper vector generation + caching to reduce cost per query.
3) Offline summarization/recap generation for itineraries and post-trip emails (batch jobs using Redwood Optimize).

Success metrics to propose for a pilot (6 weeks):
- Latency: 95th percentile under 200ms for response start for chat flows (target 150ms if we can get infra close).
- Cost: reduce per-1k-token spend by >= 30% vs their current hosted provider baseline (we'll baseline in week 0).
- Reliability: fewer rate-limit incidents and 99.5% uptime for the pilot routes.
- Quality: no measurable regression on 5 canonical prompts (we'll run eval harness).

Outbound sequences (short + test variants):
- Subject A: "Cut chat latency by 30% for Pemberton TravelOps support"
- Subject B: "Pilot: predictable LLM latency & lower token costs for travel teams"
- First email body (short):
  Hi Leah — quick note: we help ops-heavy travel SaaS (Booking/Itinerary products) get predictable, low-latency LLM responses and lower token spend without re-architecting your stack. Example: one customer moved to dedicated inference and cut median response start by 40% while reducing token spend through caching/quantization. Can we set a 20-minute call to explore a 6-week pilot?

- Follow-up (if no reply):
  Quick follow-up — happy to share a short benchmark on a sample prompt from your help center if you can paste one line. No commitment.

Call / discovery script (30 minutes):
- 0–5: intros + 1-sentence company positioning (we help make LLMs predictable & cheap in prod).
- 5–12: current stack + traffic patterns (tokens/day, spikes, p95 latency they see).
- 12–20: concrete flows they care about (chat, search, batch jobs). Ask: "Which flow would you prioritize for a 6-week pilot?"
- 20–26: constraints: data residency, KMS, HIPAA/PCI adjacency?
- 26–30: propose next step: pilot scope doc + ask for sample prompt + engineering contact.

Discovery questions to prioritize:
- What provider(s) are you using now? volume? cost per month?
- Target latency SLOs for chat / search? 95p and median?
- Any restrictions (air-gapped, VPC-only, KMS)?
- Typical sequence lengths for chat (tokens in/out)?
- Do you use embeddings for search today? refresh cadence?

Objections + suggested responses (rough):
- "We already use X managed API and it’s simpler" → A: totally — Redwood can sit behind the same SDK pattern and show a targeted pilot on one route; low engineering lift, measurable results (latency/cost).
- "Cost is unpredictable" → A: we propose Dedicated or controlled routing + batching and transparent token breakdowns; pilot includes a cost baseline and automated suggestions (Optimize).
- "We need our data to stay in our VPC" → A: Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and on-prem options with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
- "Integration effort is too high" → A: 1-2 day SDK + route config prototype for the pilot; Solutions Eng will pair-program and ship a minimal route.

Pilot plan (6-week, lightweight):
- Week 0: baseline collection (we get sample prompts / telemetry + baseline cost/latency).
- Week 1: move one chat route to Redwood hosted/Dedicated with canary rollout (engineer pairing).
- Week 2–3: tune batching/caching; set up Optimize recommendations; run initial evals.
- Week 4: run cost experiments (quantization where appropriate) and measure quality/regression.
- Week 5–6: finalize runbook for production handover + SLA discussion.

Engineering notes (prep items for us):
- Need a canonical prompt from their help center (1–3 examples).
- Ask for p95/p50 numbers from current provider + tokens per request distribution.
- Confirm whether embedding vectors are stored in-house (Milvus/FAISS) or via managed vector DB.

Personal next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Find Leah Armstrong email (LinkedIn + Clearbit) — ACTION: Jordan to intro if LinkedIn connection exists.
- [ ] Draft intro email + one-pager tailored to travel use case (Maya).
- [ ] Create a quick benchmark harness with a travel help-center prompt (Priya).
- [ ] Prepare pilot SOW template and cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private options.

Notes / Quick hypotheses to test in outreach:
- Travel companies care more about response start latency than overall token generation duration (because UX suffers while waiting for first word). Emphasize streaming + early token start improvements.
- Offer a non-committal micro-benchmark (we run 10 sample prompts and return p95/p50/cost) — low friction.

Raw outbound drafts (play with tone):
- Casual variant:
  Subject: "Quick: latency + cost pilots for travel chat"
  Body: "Leah — I’ll be brief. Redwood helps travel teams get faster chat responses and lower token bills without ripping out your stack. 20-min intro + we’ll run a free 10-prompt benchmark. Interested?"

- More formal variant:
  Subject: "Pilot proposal: predictable LLM inference for Pemberton TravelOps"
  Body: "Leah — We help platform teams deliver predictable LLM latency, clear unit economics, and compliant deployments. If you’re open to a short pilot we’ll baseline your current routes and deliver concrete latency and cost improvements in 6 weeks.\n\n  Attached: outline of pilot scope and typical metrics."

Potential signal triggers for escalation to AE / Solutions Eng:
- They report p95 > 400ms or frequent rate limits.
- They say embeddings cost is > 30% of their monthly model spend.
- They need KMS + SLA within 2 months.

Logistics / internal asks:
- Jordan: try for warm intro to Leah this week.
- Priya: assemble 1-page travel-specific benchmark doc + 2 example prompts.
- Maya: draft pilot SOW and calendar availability for next 6 weeks.

Random scratch thoughts (unpolished):
- Could pitch a cost-split for initial weeks if they’re extremely price sensitive (we cover infra for weeks 1–2).
- Consider guest blog/case study angle if pilot reaches production quickly — travel stories are good for marketing.
- Keep the first demo very visual: streaming latency demo, token cost dashboard, and an SLO chart.

End of doc.
